application question

**Why would you like to volunteer with The Cyber Helpline, and what would you bring to this role?**

I want to volunteer because this is the part of cybersecurity that sits closest to the person on the other end. Most security work protects systems. This role protects someone's savings, their photos, their sense of safety, and it does that by explaining what happened in plain language and helping them take the next step. That is the kind of work I want to be good at.

I bring a technical foundation and experience talking to non-technical people under pressure. I completed an MSc in Information Security at Royal Holloway, University of London, studying security management, cryptography, secure business architectures, digital forensics and network security, and I hold CompTIA Security+ and ISC2 CC. My projects are about exactly the problems your service users face. I built InboxDefender, a Python phishing-analysis tool that processes real email data and maps indicators to MITRE ATT&CK, and SafePaste, a Chrome extension that detects sensitive data patterns in pasted content. I also built AttackSurfaceIQ, which analyses Windows Event Logs to identify endpoint risks.

In my current role as IT Support Assistant at The Colourful Aura I am the first point of contact for 15 employees across 15–20 devices. I investigate suspicious emails, manage Active Directory access, troubleshoot endpoint problems and write technical documentation. As Person in Charge at The Co-operative Group I run weekly risk assessments, document incidents and coordinate 7–8 colleagues per shift. Both roles have taught me to listen carefully, stay calm when someone is stressed, and explain a technical problem without jargon.

I can commit the four cases a week across 42 weeks, I am based in the UK, and I have a quiet place to work with a reliable internet connection. I would take the training seriously and I would rather ask a question than give someone advice I am not sure about.

I am an MSc Information Security graduate with CompTIA Security+ and ISC2 CC. I work in IT support, where I handle access requests, investigate suspicious emails and keep documentation ready for audit. I have also built my own security tools in Python and JavaScript.

I volunteer because I want security work to reach people who cannot afford it. I am organised, careful with sensitive information and good at explaining technical problems in plain language. I can commit a few hours each week and I am keen to build real ISO 27001 experience.
Describe the causes you are interested in or the kinds of roles you’d like to take on

I am interested in causes that support people who are vulnerable, including mental health, bereavement and community services. I want to help them keep their systems and records safe so they can focus on the people they support.

I would like roles where I can handle access reviews, keep risk and incident records accurate, gather audit evidence and help with cyber awareness. I work best where I can take ownership of a small set of tasks, keep them tidy and explain them clearly to people who are not technical.
